title: Sharp Circular Sampling and Derivative Period Polynomials
summary: We determine the exact maximal reflected zero region that forces centered binomial samples of a balanced entire function to have all zeros on the unit circle. In degree $d\ge2$, this region is \[ Ω_d=\left\{a+ib:\ a^2-\frac{b^2}{d-1}\le\frac d4\right\}. \] The finite theorem is sharp already for a single reflected zero pair, and a phase-preserving canonical-product approximation extends it to balanced entire functions of order at most one. De Bruijn strip contraction and projective Hermite--Kakeya--Obreschkoff theory then give the exact common-zero obstruction, simplicity, strict interlacing…
